tier_reason: The megabunny README 'My results' table lists SFML 12.4, Raylib (C) 9.6 and SDL2 opengl 21.9 mbunnies/s, and the code is public (sfml/main.cpp, raylib/main.c, sdl2/main.c with run.sh using g++/gcc -O3), but no CPU, GPU, driver, compiler version or library version is stated and the suite is a 3-star hobby repo, so it is neither A nor B.

corrections.caveats: Third-party hobby benchmark (electronstudio/megabunny, 3 stars, GPL-3.0, 6 commits; SFML added 2024-05-12, last commit 2024-11-05) with no CPU or GPU model, no driver, no compiler version and no library versions; one run per program, no repetitions. The README itself says the benchmark is not a good reason to choose a framework. The baseline is off-category: raylib and SDL2 are GPU sprite/game frameworks, not the rasterizers-2d baselines (Skia, Cairo, Blend2D), and SFML itself is a multimedia framework whose 2D drawing is GPU sprite submission rather than vector rasterization, so the category fit is weak. The measured code uses the SFML 2.x API (two-argument sf::VideoMode, default-constructed sf::Sprite with setTexture), which does not compile against the current SFML 3.x, so the numbers describe an unstated SFML 2.x release. Workload differences: SFML calls window.draw once per sprite, raylib batches DrawTexture internally and also calls DrawFPS each frame, SDL2 sets SDL_HINT_RENDER_BATCHING and fills its 1M-entry rect array inside the timed region; the bunny texture is 32x32, so SDL2's 32x32 destination rects match the texture size the other two draw (draw sizes are equivalent). Vsync is not requested by any program and is immaterial at roughly 10-22 frames per second. The timer includes first-frame costs. The table labels SFML as language 'C' because the printf string in main.cpp hard-codes it. SFML loses to SDL2 in the same table (about 0.57x, derived from page data), so this is only a win over raylib. No SFML-owned benchmark exists in the SFML repo (README, no benchmark directory). An old first-party SFML forum benchmark (2007, topic 43 on en.sfml-dev.org) reported SFML 3366% faster than SDL 1.2 on 2000 static sprites and 9233% on rotating sprites; that page is blocked here (WebSearch snippet only), SDL 1.2 is obsolete, and critics noted it compared SDL's software rendering against hardware-accelerated SFML, so it is not usable evidence.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: From the benchmark's run.sh scripts: g++ -O3 for the SFML program (pkg-config sfml-all), gcc -O3 for the raylib and SDL2 programs; compiler versions, the SFML 2.x / raylib / SDL2 versions and their own build flags are not stated (setup.sh prints gcc --version but no output is recorded).
corrections.workload: Megabunny: draw one million identical static 32x32 bunny sprites per frame (one per pixel position of a 1000x1000 window) for 100 frames, reported as millions of bunnies per second (gettimeofday around the whole draw loop, including clear and present).

notes: Numbers and the 1.29x (12.4/9.6) and 0.57x (12.4/21.9) ratios are correct and derived from page data; metadata checked (Zlib, 12.1k stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-10-06 'Add a debug postfix to libssh2'). Shortcomings to record: off-category baseline (raylib, not Skia/Cairo/Blend2D) and weak rasterizers-2d fit, hobby benchmark without hardware or versions, measured SFML 2.x not current 3.x, slower than SDL2 in the same table. Corrected the record's caveat that SDL2 draws a different size: bunny.png is 32x32, so the draw sizes match.
